newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Moslem opposition member detained.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Moslem opposition member detained.

text.p: Bosnian police on Wednesday detained a Moslem opposition politician who once helped lead an armed rebellion against the Bosnian government, an interior ministry official said.

Ibrahim Djedovic was detained during a session of the Moslem-Croat federation parliament, where he serves as an elected deputy with an opposition party, said Suad Arnautovic, a deputy in the interior ministry.
The authorities planned to charge Djedovic for alleged war crimes committed during the 1992-95 war in Bosnia, Arnautovic told Reuters.
Djedovic is known as an ally of rebel Moslem leader Fikret Abdic, who fought an unsuccessful rebellion against the Sarajevo government during the Yugoslav conflict.
Abdic, a prosperous businessman, declared the northwest Bihac region an autonomous province and formed alliances with separatist Serbs and Croats against the Bosnian government army.
Abdic's rebellion collapsed in 1995 and he and his followers fled to neighbouring Croatia.
Djedovic, a member of Abdic's opposition party, was later allowed to return to the parliament building and authorities said they wanted deputies to vote to remove his parliamentary immunity.
Under the terms of a peace treaty and negotiations beteen rival ethnic leaders, Bosnian federation or Serb authorities have the right to prosecute alleged war criminals.
But arrests have to be screened by the U.N. war crimes tribunal which decides if the authorities have met minimum international legal standards.
Arnautovic said the Hague-based tribunal had given the interior ministry the green light to prosecute Djedovic.
"We have got the approval of the Hague (to prosecute). The Hague has all the documentation and evidence about war crimes committed by Djedovic," he said.
Tribunal representatives in Sarajevo were not available for comment.
